order.why_here: Smallest tracker there is: a queue plus a running sum, and the habit of updating state by what enters and what leaves.
Same stream, now keyed: one hash map entry per message holding the only fact that matters, its next allowed time.
Back to the queue, but the window is measured in time not count, so eviction becomes a while-loop and same-time hits get merged.
Opens the box we have been using: buckets, chaining and load-factor resizing explain why a dict lookup is O(1) on average.
First true combination of two parts: an array for random access plus an index map, joined by swap-with-last deletion.
An array and a cursor; teaches that clearing data can be a bound you move instead of work you do.
Two maps with two lifetimes: short-lived in-flight state and forever-aggregated statistics compressed to (sum, count).
Keep every version instead of the latest one; a sorted list per key plus bisect answers 'value as of time t'.
Same versioned-list idea applied per index, with snapshot ids as the clock, so a snapshot costs O(1) instead of O(n).
Lazy global flag: record a flip instead of performing it, and maintain the count so every query is O(1).
The classic combination: hash map for lookup plus doubly linked list for recency order, every operation O(1).
LRU inside each frequency bucket plus a min-frequency pointer; the hardest bookkeeping of the hash-map-plus-list family.
Buckets of keys by count chained in a linked list so both the max and the min key are always at the ends.
Frequency buckets as stacks with a max pointer; ties broken by recency for free because a key lives in every lower bucket too.
List of stacks plus a min-heap of indices with room, using lazy deletion to skip heap entries that went stale.
Sorted disjoint intervals maintained with bisect; inserting a point may extend or merge neighbours.
Same sorted-interval structure but with range add and range remove that split and swallow intervals.
When updates and range sums interleave, a 2D Fenwick tree turns both into O(log m * log n).
Value to sorted positions plus bisect counts occurrences in any range; random sampling finds the candidate.
Several ordered views of the same records kept as heaps, with lazy deletion by version stamp to stay consistent.
A trie of path components: the tracker is a tree whose edges are directory names.
Build the ordered structure itself: sorted linked lists stacked into random express lanes for expected O(log n) search.
